label: Start of recall when the next two outputs are from {w,0,t,q,2,a,g}
explanation: Low end of candidate unit 67. It fires mostly at the start of the output phase: the <DEL> step holds about 50% of activation mass (5.3x lift) and recall_idx 1-2 hold about 31%. After recall_idx 3 it is almost never active, and it never fires at t=0-1. Whether it fires depends on which tokens are coming up. It is strongly tied to the next outputs being one of w (14x lift as out_tok), 0, t, q, 2, a or g, and is strongest when the sequence starts with w. The top examples are almost all <DEL> steps in sequences that open with w (e.g. w w w u -> 1.00). The predicate requires the current and next output to both be in that set during recall_idx 0-2. It reaches only about 0.30 precision and 0.37 recall (0.45 of activation mass) on dev, so the token preference is graded, not a clean set. About 15% of mass comes from weak original-phase firing near the end of the input, which this predicate does not capture. It does not depend on the input token itself, apart from <DEL>.
